I have just under a thousand hours of gameplay in kerbal and I love it. The game isn't for everyone though, it has a pretty steep learning curve that can be a bit frustrating at first. There is a pretty good mod community around it, and the devs seem to be updating and adding features to it still. It is a sim game however, you'll have to actually fly the contraptions you create. So if you like flight sims then you'll love this game, even if it isn't a hardcore sim.

It's a really fun game that takes a bit to get use to. The first time you can get a proper orbit is an awesome feeling. Once you are able to get to other planets and do orbital slingshots with ease, there are still a lot of challenges people have come up with. Scott Manley really helped me out with learning the game. He does some cool builds and explains the physics of the game and rockets really well (plus he has an awesome voice).

I would probably start with career mode to learn the basic rocket engines and designs that you can get into orbit with. There are some cool mods that increase difficulty like real physics, using our solar system to proper scale, and a few that add extra planetary bodies.

Overall I'd say its worth the cost right now.
